s1.syndrome_frame: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding with a gastric mass and anemia
salient_findings: Heterogeneous mass with fat attenuation and internal septations on CT
key_facts: Approximately 1 year of upper gastrointestinal bleeding
No prior evaluations
Referred for upper endoscopy
Large antral mass found on endoscopy
Mucosal biopsy was obtained
Declined endoscopic ultrasound initially
Lost to follow-up during pregnancy
Returned with ongoing anemia and new epigastric pain
Repeat esophagogastroduodenoscopy with endoscopic ultrasound identified a 6 cm mass
Mass arose from the muscularis propria of the gastric antrum
CT demonstrated a 9.7 × 7.8 × 4.8 cm heterogeneous mass
Mass was adherent to the posterior wall of the gastric antrum
Mass had predominantly fat attenuation and internal septations
No pathologic lymphadenopathy
Presented with melena
Biopsy results were consistent with adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass had predominantly fat attenuation and biopsy results were consistent with adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Large antral mass found on endoscopy and mass arose from the muscularis propria of the gastric antrum

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass had internal septations and was heterogeneous on CT

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass arose from the muscularis propria of the gastric antrum and was a large antral mass

shortlist.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Mass had predominantly fat attenuation and was large in size

raw.rationale: The biopsy results were consistent with adipose tissue and the mass had predominantly fat attenuation on CT, which is consistent with a lipoma.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors typically do not have predominantly fat attenuation on CT and are more likely to have pathologic lymphadenopathy.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are malignant tumors that would likely have more aggressive features and pathologic lymphadenopathy, which were not present in this case.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are smooth muscle tumors that would not have predominantly fat attenuation on CT and would not be consistent with biopsy results showing adipose tissue.

rejected.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
rejected.why: Atypical lipomatous tumors are large, deep-seated lipomas that can have a more complex appearance on imaging, but the presence of internal septations and the size of the mass in this case could still be consistent with a large lipoma, and the biopsy results were consistent with adipose tissue.
